# northflank_job (Data Source)

Looks up a job in a Northflank project, either by its `id` or by its `name`. Set exactly one of them.

The API does not report which image or build service a job runs, nor its runtime environment, so those are not available here.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# By ID.
data "northflank_job" "by_id" {
  project_id = "my-application"
  id         = "nightly-report"
}

# By name.
data "northflank_job" "by_name" {
  project_id = "my-application"
  name       = "Nightly Report"
}

output "nightly_schedule" {
  value = data.northflank_job.by_name.cron.schedule
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_id` (String) ID of the project the job belongs to.

### Optional

- `id` (String) Identifier of the job. Set this to look the job up by ID.
- `name` (String) Name of the job. Set this to look the job up by name, which lists the project's jobs to find it.

### Read-Only

- `active_deadline_seconds` (Number) Longest a run may take, in seconds. Null when Northflank's own limit applies.
- `app_id` (String) Full identifier Northflank uses for the job's deployment.
- `backoff_limit` (Number) Number of times a failed run is retried.
- `command` (String) Command override. Null when the image's `CMD` is used.
- `created_at` (String) Creation time, in RFC 3339 format.
- `cron` (Attributes) The job's schedule. Null for a manual job. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cron))
- `deployment_plan` (String) ID of the compute plan each job run uses.
- `description` (String) Short description of the job.
- `entrypoint` (String) Entrypoint override. Null when the image's `ENTRYPOINT` is used.
- `job_type` (String) `cron` or `manual`.
- `suspended` (Boolean) Whether a cron job's schedule is currently suspended.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags attached to the job.
- `uid` (String) Permanent identifier of the job. Unlike `id`, it never changes and is never reused.

<a id="nestedatt--cron"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cron`

Read-Only:

- `concurrency_policy` (String) `allow`, `forbid` or `replace`.
- `schedule` (String) Cron expression.
